records.english: Thus it is that--once we have received our empowerment--we must then carefully observe that fine line that separates an action which becomes a downfall from one which does not.  As such, a disciple must first go to their Lama and receive an explanation of the guidelines for these vows, and learn them well.  This is necessary because it is improper to hear all the tantric commitments in their entirety prior to receiving empowerment. ***

records.acip: DE LTA NA MNGON PAR BYANG CHUB PA'I BSHAD PA LAS, LAG LEN GYI RIM PA NI DBANG GSUM PA BSKUR PA'I MJUG THOGS NYID DU DBANG BZHI PA BSKUR BA YIN NO, DE LTA MA YIN NA DBANG BZHI PA MA BSKUR PA'I SNGA ROL TU CHU LAS NYA LDANG BA'I TSUL DU ZUNG 'JUG GI SKUR BZHENGS PA'I TSUL BSHAD PA'I SKYON YOD DO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA DANG 'GAL PAR 'GYUR RAM SNYAM PAS, RJE'I DGONGS PAR GANG SONG BLO LDAN RNAMS KYIS DPYOD DGOS KYI, RMONGS BRTUL BDAG LTA BUS KHA TSON GCOD DKA' BA'I GNAS SU SNANG NGO,

records.english: If we explain it this way though it seems to me that we'd contradict the statement from the Treatise on Becoming Enlightened, where it says-- The steps that we go through here, in actual practice, are that immediately after the third empowerment has been granted the fourth is granted.  Describing it in any other way would raise the problem that one would have to rise up in the holy body of the combination of the two--as a fish suddenly jumps out of the water--even before the fourth empowerment had been granted. Deciding then which of these positions is really what the Lord himself had in mind is something that those of you with real intelligence are going to need to figure out.  This seems to be a point that someone as dull and ignorant as myself would have trouble making a definitive decision about.

records.wylie: [e19] phyogs snga ma 'gog pa ni, 'dod pa'i rten can gyi so so skye bo gcig gi rgyud la rnam shes du ma gcig car skye ba yod de, de 'dra ba'i skyo {%so} skye la gzugs sogs yul drug nye bar gnas shing, tshogs drug ga'i rgyu rkyen sa bon dang mig sogs dbang po drug dang, yul drug la nye ring med pa'i yid byed tshogs drug ga'i de ma thag rkyen byed nus pa zhig stobs che chung med par tshogs pa na, de'i mjug thogs su tshogs drug ka gcig car skye ba ma gtogs tshogs drug las dang por de nyid skye zhes pa'i khyad par mi rung ba'i phyir te, rgyu tshogs tshang ba la khyad par med pa'i phyir ro
records.english: Here is how they would refute the opposite position here: It is indeed the case that multiple types of consciousness can arise, all at the same time, in the mind of a normal being with a body and mind based in the desire realm. And that's because of the following.  Suppose that—for this particular kind of normal being—specific entities which possess the capacity to act as immediate conditions for all six of the different types of consciousness come together, without any distinction where one is stronger than another. That is, first of all, the six objects of the senses—visible forms and such—are close at hand; and moreover the causes and conditions for all six types of consciousness are also present—the requisite mental seeds, and the six sense powers of the eye and so on.  Finally, the mind is turning to the six objects of these senses, without one being closer or another being farther. In such an instance, all six consciousnesses of the collection must arise, in the next moment, all together.  It would be a problem at this juncture if you tried to draw a distinction: if you said that only a certain one of the six arose, before any of the others. That in turn is true because there is no distinction between any of these six with regard to all the necessary causes assembling for it to arise.

records.english: As such—because they don't see the results of their giving in a direct way—there is a possibility that they will fail to engage in the act of giving.
